title: inference-data-flow-deidentification-and-audit-correlation-standards-2026
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines standards for handling inference request data in Redwood Inference environments where data residency, deidentification, and auditable correlations between logs and persisted evidence are required. It covers: classification and transformation rules applied at edge and ingestion, the canonical audit log schema used across hosted/dedicated/private deployments, retention and archival policies, and an auditable evidence-packaging procedure for regulatory and internal reviews.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all components that process or log inference requests and responses, including:
- API gateway / ingress proxies (hosted & dedicated)
- Request preprocessor and prompt normalization services
- Serving runtime (tokenizer, KV cache, model executor) where request metadata is captured
- Observability pipelines (audit-log collectors, immutable stores, SIEM/EDR integrations)
- Private deployment agents (on-prem VMs, VPC connectors)

Exclusions: downstream customer systems outside Redwood-managed control (customers remain responsible for their own downstream retention policies).

Owner and stakeholders
----------------------
- Document owner: Security (Asha Patel)
- Primary stakeholders: Product (Model-serving & Private), Eng Infra, Eng SRE, Compliance, Legal

Background and rationale
------------------------
Regulatory regimes increasingly require two capabilities for inference platforms: (1) strong controls that remove or mask personal data prior to persistent storage or cross-border transit; and (2) an auditable link between transient request handling and retained evidence used in audits or incident investigations. Historically, logs captured rich request payloads which created residency and PII exposure. This standard shifts our platform to a minimally sufficient logging model with deterministic correlation primitives to reconstruct request context when permitted.

Principles
----------
1. Minimize: retain the least amount of user-identifiable information absolutely required for operations and compliance.
2. Localize: enforce residency constraints at the ingress layer; do not move raw customer content across regions without a documented, approved exception.
3. Correlate, don’t duplicate: store immutable audit tokens that allow rehydration of context only through an evidence packaging workflow.
4. Immutable audit trail: all actions that transform, mask, or route data must be logged with verifiable metadata and signer identity.

Data classification and allowed transformations
---------------------------------------------
Each inference request must be annotated with a classification label before it reaches long-term stores:
- classification: [public, internal, sensitive, regulated]
Rules:
- public: no masking required; logs may contain non-PII payload excerpts for short-term operational debugging (T=7 days).
- internal: redact user identifiers and tokens; keep payload hashes for dedup and caching (T=30 days).
- sensitive: strip PII (names, emails, phone numbers) using the DeID pipeline (see DeID rules below); replace with deterministic salt-hashed tokens.
- regulated: do not persist any content outside the originating region. Only store audit tokens and control-plane metadata (no plaintext).

Deidentification (DeID) pipeline
-------------------------------
Overview: DeID runs as an ingress transform service with these stages:
1) Tokenization: identify tokens matching PII entity types using our NER models and regex fallback.
2) Deterministic masking: replace identified tokens with salt-hashed placeholders (SHA256 with per-tenant salt stored in KMS).
3) Structural redaction: for structured inputs (JSON documents) apply schema-based redaction rules so keys and types are preserved.
4) Fingerprinting: compute and persist a content fingerprint (SHA256) for caching and dedup correlation.

Implementation details:
- Per-tenant salt rotation schedule: rotate every 90 days; rotation must create new salt versions but keep previous salts available for rehydration under approval for 180 days.
- DeID library versions must be recorded in the audit metadata: deid_version and model_ner_version.

Canonical audit log schema
-------------------------
All components writing to the audit pipeline must emit a consistent JSON envelope. Example minimal schema (fields explained below):
{\n  "audit_id": "string: uuid v4",\n  "ts": "RFC3339 timestamp",\n  "env": "region or cluster id",\n  "service": "service-name",\n  "principal": "service/user identity (OIDC sub)",\n  "action": "ingest|transform|route|persist|access|delete",\n  "classification": "public|internal|sensitive|regulated",\n  "deid_ops": "list of applied operations or empty",\n  "fingerprint": "sha256 hex",\n  "evidence_token": "opaque short token (10 chars)",\n  "retention_tier": "hot|warm|cold|immutable",\n  "reference": "s3://... or immutable-store://... OR redaction rule id",\n  "signature": "kms-sig or hmac for non-repudiation"\n}

Notes on fields:
- evidence_token: short nonce that ties this log record to an evidence bundle. The token is recorded in the immutable log stream (retained per retention policy) while the full payload is stored only in the evidence vault under restricted access. Evidence tokens are generated by central token service with monotonic sequence per tenant.
- signature: every audit record must be signed by the emitting service’s signing key (CA-managed) so records are non-repudiable.

Retention matrix and regional residency rules
--------------------------------------------
Retention decisions derive from classification and regulatory mapping. Example matrix: (presented as human-readable rows)
- public: logs hot=7d, warm=30d, cold=90d; location: global aggregated permitted.
- internal: hot=30d, warm=180d; location: stored in origin region; aggregated anonymized metrics allowed cross-region.
- sensitive: hot=7d (masked), immutable evidence vault=365d; location: origin region only.
- regulated: no cross-border transit; logs contain only audit tokens and control-plane metadata; evidence vault kept in-region; retention per contract (typically 7–10 years).

All retention tiers must map to technical storage classes and be enforceable by lifecycle policies in the ingestion pipeline (S3 lifecycle rules, object locks for immutable tier, or WORM stores).

Evidence vault and packaging for audits
-------------------------------------
Purpose: provide a controlled method to retrieve complete inference request context (raw request, deid operations, salts used, operator approvals) for auditors or incident responders under an approval workflow.

Evidence bundle components:
- bundle metadata (audit_id, requester, purpose, approval ticket id)
- signed transform chain (list of deid ops with timestamps and versions)
- per-tenant salt version manifest (KMS key ids, rotation history)
- raw request and response (if permitted), else deid-transformed copy plus fingerprint mapping
- system provenance logs (service-level transaction logs, routing decisions)
- access control list and audit trail showing who accessed the bundle

Packaging workflow (high level):
1) Request: Compliance files evidence request in internal ticketing system and attaches justification and scope.
2) Approval: Legal & Security approvers must sign the request. Approval records become part of the bundle.
3) Assemble: Evidence assembler service retrieves matching items by audit_token and constructs a signed bundle.
4) Seal: Bundle is encrypted with a per-request ephemeral envelope key, which is itself encrypted with auditors’ public key (or KMS-protected service key for internal reviewers).
5) Access: Bundle is made available in a secure temporary location for N days (default N=7). All accesses logged and require MFA.
6) Audit: After review, the bundle is archived (immutable) or shredded according to the request outcome.

Operational runbooks and example procedures
------------------------------------------
Procedure: Validate DeID pipeline after a release (SRE + Security)
1) Create synthetic test tenant with samples covering all classification tiers.
2) Run ingestion through staged DeID pipeline.
3) Confirm output fingerprints match expected values.
4) Inspect audit logs: verify audit_id, deid_version, evidence_token, and signature presence.
5) Trigger evidence packaging for a sample audit_id and validate bundle contents and access controls.
6) Promote only if all checks pass.

Procedure: Incident triage where regulated content may have been exported
1) Immediately rotate per-tenant salts and mark all affected salt-versions as revoked.
2) Create high-priority evidence request for relevant audit_tokens.
3) Freeze exports in origin region while forensic collection runs.
4) Notify Legal and Compliance within 1 hour.
5) Package bundle and provide to authorized investigators under sealed access.

Audit-friendly log examples and CLI snippets
-------------------------------------------
Example audit record (single-line JSON):
{"audit_id":"d2f2e8a4-9bca-4cd1-8f0b-1b2aa7e2f7c3","ts":"2026-10-02T14:12:31Z","env":"us-west-2","service":"ingress-deid","principal":"svc-ingress@redwood.internal","action":"transform","classification":"sensitive","deid_ops":"ner-v2.1;mask-v2026-05","fingerprint":"b3d5c...af2","evidence_token":"EVD-7G4J2","retention_tier":"immutable","reference":"immutable://evidence/evid-2026-10-02/d2f2e8","signature":"kms:v1:SIG..."}

CLI: request evidence (internal tool)
$ rwd-evidence request --token EVD-7G4J2 --reason "Regulatory audit: CN payroll samples" --approvers "legal@redwood.com,security@redwood.com"

Non-repudiation and key management
----------------------------------
- All service signing keys must be provisioned via CA and rotated every 180 days.
- KMS access for salt retrieval must be guarded by IP and role conditions; requests for salt material for rehydration require two-person approval (security + compliance).
- Evidence assembler and archive operations are logged to an immutable store with object-lock enabled where regulations require.

Integration with Incident Response and Secure SDLC
-------------------------------------------------
- Any change to DeID or audit schemas must be submitted as an ADR and accompany a test plan that validates backward compatibility of evidence_token correlation and bundle assembly.
- On-call SRE and security responders must have a runbook describing how to request bundles, escalate approvals, and preserve chain-of-custody.

Metrics and monitoring
---------------------
Key telemetry to publish to dashboards:
- DeID coverage: % of requests classified and processed successfully (SLO 99.9%).
- Audit record integrity failures: count of records missing signature or essential fields (alert at >5/hr).
- Evidence assembly lead time: median time from request to sealed bundle (SLO median < 2 hours for priority requests).
- Salt rotation lag: fraction of tenants beyond rotation window.

Governance and exceptions
-------------------------
- Exceptions: Any deviation from residency rules requires an exception request stored in the exceptions register with compensating controls declared.
- Exception lifetime: max 90 days; automated expiry and review required.

Appendix A: DeID regex and NER heuristics (summary)
--------------------------------------------------
- Email: \b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b
- Phone: \b\+?[0-9 \-().]{7,}\b
- SSN-like: \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b
- NER: use ner-v2.1 for EN/ES, fallback to regexes for high-confidence matches; low-confidence matches are logged to a review queue (retained 7 days).

Appendix B: Example staging test checklist
------------------------------------------
- Synthetic dataset: 1k requests covering public/internal/sensitive/reg.
- Confirm lifecycle policies applied to S3 prefixes.
- Run retention sweep job and confirm objects move to correct tier.
- Simulate evidence request and validate access controls.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
-------------------------------
Q: When can raw requests be exported to a third party?
A: Only under an approved contract clause and explicit evidence request. Any cross-border transit must be approved by Legal and recorded in the exceptions register.

Q: Who can request salt material for rehydration?
A: Security and Compliance staff via two-person approval. Requests are time-bound and logged into the evidence bundle.
